stories.headline: Denver named finalist for 2028 Democratic National Convention alongside Boston and Philadelphia
stories.summary:
Denver is one of three cities remaining under consideration to host the 2028 Democratic National Convention after the Democratic National Committee narrowed its list Thursday, dropping Atlanta and Chicago. The convention is scheduled for Aug. 7-10, 2028, and a final decision is expected later this year. Republicans have already selected Houston for their 2028 convention.

Denver last hosted the Democratic National Convention in 2008, when then-Sen. Barack Obama accepted his party's presidential nomination at Mile High Stadium. Mayor Mike Johnston said the earlier convention 'proved what this city could do' and called another hosting opportunity 'a tremendous opportunity for everyone who calls Denver home.'

DNC Chairman Ken Martin praised all three cities for submitting 'incredibly strong bids.' City officials have previously said the convention would be an 'enormous economic boon for Denver,' drawing an estimated 50,000 visitors for the four-day event. No fundraising target has been set yet, though early conversations on that front have begun.

stories.headline: Federal judge blocks Colorado law requiring regular inspections of Aurora immigrant detention center
stories.summary:
A federal judge in Denver on Thursday blocked the core provisions of House Bill 1276, a state law passed by Democratic legislators this year requiring unannounced health inspections at least once every three months at the GEO Group-operated Aurora immigrant detention center. U.S. District Court Judge Daniel D. Domenico ruled the inspection requirements were likely preempted by federal law and GEO's existing contract with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

Domenico set the injunction to expire Oct. 15, when GEO's current ICE contract is due to expire, noting that terms of any new contract could alter the legal analysis significantly. He left intact county officials' existing discretionary inspection authority and did not block other provisions of HB 1276 related to medical staffing and infectious disease inspections, which the state said are not yet in effect.

Attorney General Phil Weiser called the ruling a 'narrow, temporary injunction,' while the Colorado Immigrant Rights Coalition expressed concern about its impact. GEO Group recently announced plans to open a second ICE-contracted detention facility in Hudson, north of Denver.

stories.headline: Colorado voters to decide on income tax cap and right to hunt and fish in November
stories.summary:
Colorado voters will weigh in this November on two citizen-initiated measures after supporters submitted enough signatures for ballot approval Thursday. Initiative 232 would cap the state's income tax rate at its current level of 4.4%, and Initiative 302 would enshrine a 'right to hunt and fish' in the state constitution.

Initiative 232 was organized by the conservative nonprofit Advance Colorado and is widely seen as an effort to neutralize a separate liberal-backed measure, Initiative 195, which would raise income taxes up to 8.4% on individuals and corporations earning more than $500,000 annually while cutting rates for lower earners. If both measures pass, legal challenges are considered likely. Initiative 195 is still awaiting ballot approval.

Initiative 302, backed by the T. Roosevelt Conservation Alliance, is a direct response to Proposition 91, which Colorado voters rejected in 2024 and which sought to ban trophy hunting of mountain lions, bobcats and lynx. Because it would amend the state constitution, Initiative 302 requires 55% voter approval to pass. Up to 14 measures may appear on the November statewide ballot.

stories.headline: Denver International Airport approves $135 million contract for North Terminal expansion
stories.summary:
Denver International Airport has approved an initial $135 million contract to begin work on a major North Terminal expansion intended to increase security capacity and international arrival facilities, with the project expected to be completed by approximately 2034. The expansion is designed to accommodate the airport's continued growth in passenger volume.

The contract represents the first phase of what is expected to be a larger capital program at DIA. The airport has been managing record or near-record passenger numbers in recent years, placing strain on existing infrastructure, particularly for international arrivals.

The announcement comes as Denver is also competing against Boston and Philadelphia to host the 2028 Democratic National Convention, with city officials citing the airport's accessibility as a key advantage in that bid.

stories.headline: Longtime Denver used bookstore The Book Rack to close after nearly 50 years
stories.summary:
The Book Rack, a used bookstore in Denver's University Hills neighborhood that has operated continuously since 1977, announced it will permanently close on Sunday, Sept. 13. Owner Cathi Kern declined to provide a reason for the closure. The store, located at 4061 E. Wesley Ave. near South Colorado Boulevard and East Iliff Avenue, describes itself as the only used bookstore to have operated continuously in Denver for that span.

Kern took over ownership three years ago. The store was included in Denver's 2025 Legacy Business Program Registry, which recognizes businesses that have operated for at least a decade. The closure announcement drew an outpouring of community response on social media, with longtime customers sharing memories and expressing regret.

The store may close earlier than Sept. 13 if its inventory sells out. It is no longer accepting books or puzzles for credit or cash. Over nearly five decades, The Book Rack offered thousands of titles across fiction and nonfiction genres, as well as gifts and puzzles, and was particularly noted for its Classics and Mystery sections.

stories.headline: Colorado settles with Cobblestone Car Wash over unfair auto-renewal practices affecting 70,000 consumers
stories.summary:
Colorado has reached a settlement with Cobblestone Car Wash over claims of unfair automatic-renewal billing practices that affected more than 70,000 consumers in the state. The settlement was announced by state officials, though specific financial terms were not detailed in initial reports.

Auto-renewal practices in subscription-style services have drawn increased regulatory scrutiny nationally and at the state level, with consumers often reporting difficulty canceling memberships or being charged without clear notice of renewal terms. Colorado's consumer protection laws require businesses to clearly disclose auto-renewal terms and provide straightforward cancellation options.

The resolution represents part of a broader state effort to enforce consumer protection statutes around subscription and membership billing practices.

stories.headline: Bo Nix set to play first preseason snaps of 2026 as Broncos host Green Bay on Friday night
stories.summary:
Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix is scheduled to make his first game appearance of the 2026 season Friday night when the Broncos host the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field at Mile High in the team's preseason home opener. Head Coach Sean Payton said Nix will play approximately 14 snaps — roughly two drives — in what will be his first live action since breaking his ankle in the divisional round playoff win over Buffalo last January.

Friday's game will also mark the first time offensive coordinator Davis Webb calls plays for Nix in a game setting. Webb said he wants to see a 'clean operation' and hopes Nix can simply enjoy being back on the field. Nix took the full set of reps throughout training camp but did not play in the Broncos' preseason opener against Atlanta, which Denver won.

Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur said quarterback Jordan Love and the Packers' starters will also see action in Denver. The Broncos enter the game having won eight consecutive preseason contests and carrying a 8-2 preseason record under Payton. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, who was nursing a muscle strain, has returned to full practice and may also see action.

stories.headline: Nuggets moving on from guard Peyton Watson after declining to sign him following qualifying offer
stories.summary:
The Denver Nuggets are moving on from guard Peyton Watson after extending him a qualifying offer at the end of July but opting not to complete a deal, according to reports. Watson averaged career-high marks last season of 14.6 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.1 blocks across 29.6 minutes per game in 54 regular-season appearances.

The decision ends Watson's tenure with Denver, where he developed significantly after being selected in the 2022 NBA Draft. His emergence as a starter-caliber player last season drew attention from other teams during the offseason.

The Nuggets' choice not to retain Watson creates a roster opening as the team prepares for the upcoming season. Further details on his next destination or the team's plans to fill his spot have not been announced.

stories.headline: Top Colorado CMAS test scores concentrated in metro Denver districts; wide gaps persist
stories.summary:
The highest-performing schools on Colorado's 2026 Measures of Academic Success standardized tests are concentrated in the Denver metro area, with top schools drawn from Denver Public Schools, Jeffco Public Schools, Adams 12 Five Star Schools, Aurora Public Schools, Cherry Creek Schools and Boulder Valley School District, according to new data released Wednesday by the Colorado Department of Education.

DPS's Polaris Elementary School retained the top spot in English language arts but slipped from first to second in math, where Aurora Quest K-8 moved to the top position. Performance gaps among metro-area districts remained stark: more than 65% of Boulder Valley students met expectations in English language arts, compared to about 7% in Sheridan School District 2, which experienced an 18-day teachers strike this spring.

In math, fewer than 4% of Sheridan School District 2 students met expectations, while 58% did in Littleton Public Schools. The Colorado Department of Education uses a scoring scale from 650 to 850, with 750 as the benchmark for meeting grade-level expectations for students in grades three through eight.

stories.headline: Sundance Film Festival to hold preview event at University of Denver in September ahead of Boulder debut
stories.summary:
The Sundance Institute announced a special event at the University of Denver's Newman Center for the Performing Arts on Sept. 8 that will offer Colorado audiences a preview of the Sundance Film Festival ahead of the festival's Colorado debut in January 2027. The event, titled 'Mostly True Stories From the Sundance Film Festival,' will feature filmmaker Amy Redford, director Rian Johnson ('Knives Out,' 'Star Wars: The Last Jedi'), director Dee Rees ('Mudbound'), producer Christine Vachon ('Past Lives') and others.

The event will explore the festival's history through the perspectives of artists who have shaped it over the decades. Tickets start at $29 for adults and $15 for students and are available online. Festival Director Eugene Hernandez said the evening will highlight 'rarely heard' stories from past festivals.

Colorado's inaugural hosting of the Sundance Film Festival is scheduled for Jan. 21-31, 2027, in Boulder. The festival is expected to bring tens of thousands of attendees to the Boulder area, and additional information on passes and tickets will be released in September.

stories.headline: DPS students return to class Monday; Denver police urge driver caution near schools
stories.summary:
Denver Public Schools students are set to begin the new academic year on Monday, Aug. 24, marking the end of summer break for the district. The Denver Police Department is using the back-to-school period to urge drivers to exercise increased caution in school zones throughout the city.

Officials are reminding motorists to observe posted speed limits near schools, watch for children crossing streets, and be alert to school buses stopping to load and unload students. Increased pedestrian activity is expected along corridors near DPS campuses beginning Monday morning.

The start of the school year follows a challenging spring for several Colorado districts. DPS's school board held a daylong retreat this week to address an internal trust breakdown among board members.

stories.headline: Stanley Marketplace marks 10th anniversary with three-day celebration in Aurora
stories.summary:
Aurora's Stanley Marketplace is celebrating its 10th anniversary this weekend with a three-day event, Aug. 21-23, called 'Stanley10,' featuring music, food tastings, artisan makers and special programming. The centerpiece 'Taste of Stanley' event on Saturday runs from 2 to 5 p.m. and includes bites from the marketplace's restaurants, beer samples and whiskey tastings, with a live jazz trio performing on the West Patio.

Tickets for Saturday's tasting are $50 and include discounts of up to 20% at participating retailers plus a Stanley Marketplace tote bag. General admission for the broader weekend events is free and open to all ages. The marketplace is located at 2501 N. Dallas St. in Aurora.

Stanley Marketplace opened a decade ago inside the 140,000-square-foot former Stanley Aviation factory and has grown into a hub of locally owned restaurants, craft breweries, boutiques and service businesses. The anniversary event underscores the venue's evolution into one of the metro area's distinctive community gathering spaces.

topStory.headline: Trump Threatens Global Economic Consequences for Nations Doing Business With Iran, Drawing Chinese Pushback
topStory.summary:
President Donald Trump announced Wednesday what he called the 'most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country,' threatening severe economic consequences against any nation whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities provide support to Iran. Writing on Truth Social, Trump declared an 'Economic D-Day' and demanded an immediate halt to oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries and front companies used to sustain Iran's economy.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reinforced the announcement Thursday, calling the effort 'the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world' and telling allies they are 'either with us or against us.' Bessent specifically called on China — Iran's largest trading partner — to 'get with the program,' while acknowledging that many conversations with Beijing are best held privately. China's Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian responded Friday that 'sanctions and pressure will not help resolve the issue' and called on all parties to pursue political and diplomatic solutions. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed the threats as a distraction from American domestic problems, while Iranian state media characterized the announcement as nothing new, noting that Tehran has spent years developing methods to circumvent economic restrictions.

The escalation follows a significant shift in U.S. strategy after weeks of nightly military strikes on Iran failed to bring Tehran back to the negotiating table. Pentagon advisers reportedly told Trump last month that the U.S. had nearly exhausted its target list in Iran and that the military campaign had reached the limits of its effectiveness, prompting the pivot toward economic pressure. The U.S. Treasury has been conducting Operation Economic Fury for months, combining targeted sanctions with a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz aimed at cutting off Iranian oil exports. Iranian crude exports have already fallen from roughly 1.3 to 1.5 million barrels per day before the war to below 300,000 barrels per day in May.

Analysts warn that enforcing Trump's threat through secondary sanctions — penalties on countries that continue buying Iranian oil — risks a direct confrontation with China at a sensitive moment in U.S.-China trade relations. Gregory Brew, a senior analyst at the Eurasia Group, noted that any new measures will need to target Iran's trading partners but said it will be 'hard for the U.S. to direct such actions at China.' Iran demonstrated the complexity of the situation this week when it finalized an oil export agreement with Tajikistan, even as the United Arab Emirates announced an indefinite trade embargo on Iran following Iranian ballistic missile strikes on its territory. The White House has not yet specified which countries or institutions will face consequences or what form those penalties will take.
